text: Since 1950, extreme natural events in the Pacific have affected over 9.2 million people and caused approximately US$3.2 billion in damage. The pilot program initially included countries like Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, and Vanuatu, with Cook Islands joining later. Although Papua New Guinea was not part of the initial insured cohort, the program's framework remains accessible for future adoption.
